name: Chisel
text: I’ll deep-dive the repo’s `src/` directory first: `find src/ -type f -name "*.py" -o -name "*.md" -o -name "*.json" -o -name "*.yaml" | wc -l` to count all candidate files. Then I’ll run `rg --type-add 'config:*.{json,yaml,yml}' -t config -t py -t md -l '.' src/` to list every file with its type, and open the top 5 largest (by `wc -c`) in parallel `vim` panes for initial triage. name: Sift
text: Sift: Hold—your `rg` command’s `--type-add` flag is brittle. It only *adds* types but doesn’t *restrict* them; so if a `.json` file contains Python code (e.g., a Jupyter notebook’s metadata), it’ll still be misclassified as `config` instead of `py`. Prove me wrong: run `rg -t py -t config -t md -t yaml --type-list | grep -E '\.(json|yaml|yml)$'` and show the overlap. Until then, your file-type mapping risks silent errors.

name: Chisel
text:
Chisel: I’ll run a strict, multi-pass file census to avoid misclassification. First, `find src/ -type f \( -name "*.py" -o -name "*.md" -o -name "*.json" -o -name "*.yaml" -o -name "*.yml" \) -printf "%f\t%p\n" | sort > src_file_list.tsv` to get every file with its full path and extension. Next, I’ll validate counts with `wc -l src_file_list.tsv` and cross-check via `ls -1 src/**/*.{py,md,json,yaml,yml} 2>/dev/null | wc -l` to ensure the two methods agree. If they diverge, I’ll diff the outputs to catch hidden files or symlinks.
